result_text:
I made a change in `xknx/devices/climate_mode.py`, but I'm not sure it fixes your case. I couldn't reproduce the "Sleep" mode, and I never found where it comes from.

The `0x21` your controller reports is binary `00100001`: the economy bit and the frost-alarm bit. xknx reads that as Economy, which Home Assistant shows as "Night". That reading looks correct, so it doesn't explain "Sleep".

I did find one real flaw. If a controller status byte has none of the four mode bits set (Comfort, Standby, Economy, Protection), xknx treats the mode as `AUTO` and overwrites the current operation mode with it. `ClimateMode._set_internal_modes_from_status` now ignores `AUTO` from the status and leaves the operation mode unchanged. The heat/cool part of the status is still applied.

I only ran the existing climate tests (88 pass). I added no test for the new behaviour, since you asked me not to touch tests.

I can't tell from the issue whether your controller sends a status byte with no mode bits on startup. After restarting Home Assistant, check the climate entity's mode against the status value in the log.
